sense.text:
Gospel means good news, good tidings, glad tidings: God's story. Early English translators linked it to God and spell, God spell, God's story. So we open up where Christ walks into the temple at the age of thirty and begins to read a portion of Isaiah.

“And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.” So he began to read on the Sabbath day. What did he read? “And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias.” Esaias is Isaiah. “And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,” and he is reading Isaiah chapter 61.

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.”

When you read verses 18 and 19, if you don't see our people in these verses, it will probably be hard, because when you're in church you're literally under a spell and you can't see yourself.

Isaiah 61 is saying the same thing as Luke 4:18, the same exact thing, so we take our time in Isaiah 61 and stop at certain points and explain it.

“And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on him. And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.”

“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek;” Good tidings is gospel, good news. So who is the gospel preached to? The meek. Look up the word meek: the term meek in the biblical context refers to an attitude of humility, gentleness, and submission to God's will. So meek doesn't mean soft. Meek means humility, gentleness, and submission to God's will. Like another scripture says, Moses was the meekest man in all Israel: he submitted to God's will 100%. We all must be meek. Meek don't mean you be soft and listen to some idiot on the street. No. It is often associated with a spirit of patience and a lack of self-assertiveness, and that ain't right; that's how most people think of it. Meekness is not to be confused with weakness. Rather, it is strength under control. Whose control? God's control. It involves a conscious choice to put others before oneself and to trust in God's sovereignty and justice. So the meek are those brothers and sisters who 100% submit themselves to the will of God.

“he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted,” Pause on brokenhearted. In the Bible, being brokenhearted means a state of deep grief, spiritual bankruptcy, and crushed spirit. You don't get no more spiritually bankrupt than black people. Recognizing one's need for God, leading to humility and repentance, where God promises to be near, heal, and restore those in this condition; often described as a shattered, wounded inner self ready for divine intervention. Emotional and spiritual ruin: intense emotional pain, despair, loss, or feeling spiritually crushed and helpless, like something shattered or torn apart. You don't get no more brokenhearted than our people. That's what slavery was about. We are a race of brokenhearted men and women. Everybody on the planet ain't brokenhearted; the social elite are not brokenhearted. Brokenhearted is our race, our people, us on the street crying for reparations. That's a broken heart right there. They said, "Pull yourself up by your bootstraps," but we can't even afford boots sometimes. In fact, not that we can't afford boots: you stole our boots. The brokenhearted is our race because we are the ones who've gone through the harshest and worst captivity, the most cruel captivity, where we even lost our language, heritage, our identity. No other people went through that.

“to proclaim liberty to the captives,” Now, if you read liberty to the captives and say that's everybody, there's something wrong with you. We're the captive race. We're the ones that were brought here against our will, shackled and chained and kept here. The hell is wrong with people talking about, "Oh no, the gospel is for everybody"? It's telling you liberty to the captives. Maybe you don't know what captive means: captive, one taken in war. Captives were often treated with great cruelty and indignity. When a city was taken by assault, all the men were slain and the women and children carried away captive and sold as slaves. How you going to read the gospel is for the captives and go, "No, the gospel is for everybody"? Everybody didn't go into captivity. You'll be on the street teaching and there's always a dumb Christian who says everybody went into slavery, all nations at one time or another went into slavery. That's a lie. When did the Chinese go into slavery? Don't tell me about the indentured servitude they were brought over here under; they got paid. Don't tell me about the East Indians that were brought over here; that's indentured servitude, that's not slavery, that's not being captive. And when did Netanyahu and his people go into slavery? World War II is not slavery. Captives were sometimes carried away into foreign countries. Is this not a foreign country? As was the case with the Jews. Boom. We are the ones that are still captive today.

“and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;” Prison: in biblical times the concept of prison and imprisonment appears in various contexts reflecting both physical and spiritual dimensions. Physical and spiritual. Christians think everything is just spiritual. No. Everything ain't just spiritual. Prisons were used as places of confinement for those awaiting trial or punishment. We are a brokenhearted and destitute people: look at the ghettos. That's become normal. That's a prison for our people, but it's so normal that that's home. Look at the war that's going on there. Our people see it as normal, and when you see your oppression as normal there's something psychologically wrong; you've been broken in your mind. Prisons also serve as powerful metaphors for spiritual bondage and deliverance, and that's how Christians use it; they keep everything right there. In the Old Testament prisons were often simple structures or even pits where individuals were detained; one of the earliest mentions is Joseph, imprisoned in Egypt.

Bound: the concept of being bound in the Bible carries both literal and metaphorical meanings, often signifying physical restraint, spiritual bondage or covenantal obligations. So it's literal and spiritual. Physical restraint, we know what that one is. Why get into the spiritual bondage now? Because the chains are off of us, and a lot of our people, if you got a good job and you make decent money, you'll be the first ones to say, "I'm not in bondage. I'm not captive. Bro, you wrong." Metaphorically, being bound can refer to spiritual bondage or the enslavement of sin; Jesus speaks of this in John 8:34. So when Christ says the truth shall make you free he's talking about two things: a literal meaning and a spiritual meaning.

precepts.why:
“(Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.)” Moses was the meekest man in all Israel. He submitted to God's will 100%. Here the term humble is often translated as meek, highlighting Moses' exemplary character in leading the Israelites with patience and reliance on God.

That is what meek means in Isaiah 61: humility, gentleness, and submission to God's will. Not soft. Meekness is strength under control, God's control. We all must be meek.

“But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.” The reward for meekness: those who are gentle and humble, who submit themselves to God's will, receive God's blessings and inherit the land.

The good tidings of Isaiah 61 are preached to these meek.

“Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.” So, blessed are the meek, those that submit themselves to God's will. Part of the Beatitudes, this statement by Christ underscores the value of meekness in the kingdom of heaven, promising eternal inheritance to those who embody this virtue.

Back to Isaiah 61:1: to preach the gospel, good tidings, unto the meek. The meek, as we just looked up, means those who submit to God's will.

“For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them,” So Christ will feed us. “and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.” All tears.

So these Israelites, our people, we would be in a constant state of being brokenhearted. That's why it says God is the one who shall wipe away all our tears from our eyes.

“And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.” There shall be no more death. Neither sorrow. Nor crying. Neither shall there be any more pain.

Former things like what? Oppression, captivity, poverty. All that's going to be done away with. So he's going to wipe away all our tears from our eyes: that is how he binds up the brokenhearted.

Liberty to the captives, because Christ spoke on that. “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword,” The Israelites shall fall by the edge of Rome's sword. “and shall be led away captive into all nations:” Highlight that word captive. Into all nations. “and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

So that didn't just stop at 70 AD. That curse continued after Rome: you had Spain, France, Britain, America. It continued, being led away captive into all nations.

Still dealing with liberty to the captives. “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them,” And God was angry with us. “and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near;” Delivered us to who? To the enemy. Where? Unto the land of the enemy, like the United States of America.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;” So King Solomon was prophesying that the Israelites would be carried away captive, and if we wanted deliverance from captivity we would have to bethink ourselves: remember who we are as a people, remember that we are the twelve tribes of Israel. We would also have to repent and make great supplication to the Lord and confess with our mouth, we have sinned, we have done perversely, we have committed wickedness. We're in that process now, each and every one of us.

Liberty to the captives. “I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will direct all his ways: he shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward, saith the Lord of hosts.” He shall let go my captives. Not for price, nor reward.

“But thus saith the Lord, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered:” During that time you had Assyria, you had Babylon. But today it's America, Spain, Portugal, Europe. They're the terrible. Even the captives of the mighty: the mighty is this white man. We're the captives. We are the prey of the terrible nations, and we shall be delivered. That's what we're talking about; that's what the scriptures are saying.

“for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.” So God says he will contend with him that contendeth with thee, meaning he's going to bring down this white man, because it's always been this white man in these last days who has contended with our race, our people. And I will save thy children.

“And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh;” How can you read this and say this is everybody that's oppressed? No. Everybody's not oppressed. “and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine:” The Lord's going to kill them. “and all flesh shall know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.” Am thy Saviour: he's not everybody's Saviour. He's the Saviour of the twelve tribes. The mighty One of Jacob: that's the Israelites right there.

“And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.” That's what's happening right now: our people are seeking, and we are finding the Lord.

“And I will be found of you, saith the Lord: and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places whither I have driven you, saith the Lord; and I will bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive.” So God said he's going to gather us from all the nations, and bring us again into the place which he caused us to be carried away captive from. Captive.

The Old Testament goes into Joseph and how he's imprisoned in Egypt; so Psalms 146. “Which executeth judgment for the oppressed: which giveth food to the hungry. The Lord looseth the prisoners:” Which executeth judgment for the oppressed: that's not everybody on the planet. So all this goes into gospel.

Start at verse 5: “Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the Lord his God: Which made heaven, and earth, the sea, and all that therein is: which keepeth truth for ever:” So remember, this is talking about the people of Jacob, because it says he's the God of Jacob. Which executeth judgment for the oppressed, letting you know that Jacob's children would be oppressed. Which giveth food to the hungry: Jacob's children would need food, physical and spiritual. The Lord looseth the prisoners: Jacob's children would be prisoners.

“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man” This is talking about Lucifer, aka the king of Babylon. So Lucifer is not a spiritual demon. Lucifer is a man. What man? The white man. That's who it's talking about; that's who Lucifer is, for you simple Christians out there with your fairy tales. “that made the earth to tremble,” How did he make the earth to tremble? With his bombs. “that did shake kingdoms;” How did he shake kingdoms? Through wars. That's not a spirit flying around dropping a bomb; that's this white man dropping bombs everywhere. He's still dropping bombs on Somalia as of last week. Then the president says he wants all the Somalians out of the country because they're garbage.

People say, "Are you mad at the Somalians?" because a lot of them say they're not black. Not mad at that. Somalians say them black Americans don't work, they don't know who their fathers are, they're no good; as soon as we come to the country we got businesses. Are the Somalians the only ones that have said that? Haitians have said it to us. Jamaicans. Puerto Ricans. Dominicans. All the tribes of our people have said that, so when the Somalians come over saying the same, here they go, same old thing. But look at Benjamin today. Look at Haiti. They up here, they reading and they learning. Oh, you love Judah now. Trump says black, get out of the country, and now they want help. The Most High said in their affliction they will seek him early.

“That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof;” That's what Lucifer has done and is doing currently. “that opened not the house of his prisoners?” This is a prison house. America is a prison house. In World War II, when the Italians were fighting against the Ethiopians, hundreds of black men went to Ethiopia to fight in the war, and America shut down all air travel to Ethiopia: "We don't want them joining with the Ethiopians." That's always been their thing. Even in the land of Israel, the American blacks are isolated from the Ethiopian blacks there, and from the blacks from Sudan or Rwanda in another area. They keep each group separate and speak ill about each group, especially the American ones. America has the same mentality: keep them separated, divide and conquer. If they unite they might overthrow us.

Still dealing with the opening of the prison house. “To open the blind eyes,” Spiritually blind. “to bring out the prisoners from the prison,” The blinded eyes of our people can't see that this is a prison, that in the United States of America we were brought here as prisoners. We did not come here willingly. The chains is evidence of that. We've always been prisoners here, but it's become so normal. Like Assata Shakur said, you got to be acutely aware that you are a slave if you want to be set free. The white man said, "Okay, let's take the chains off now," and you go, "Free at last, free at last, thank God Almighty." No, you're not free. You are still in someone else's land, following their rules, their laws. This is not freedom.

The prison are those lands where we were made captive in: not just America, but all the lands we were sent to. “and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” And we sit in darkness, and he is to bring us out of this prison house. So that's not talking about everybody on the planet.

“As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant” The blood of thy covenant is Christ dying on the cross. “I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit” God will send forth the prisoners out of the pit. America, and the various countries we're scattered in, is the pit. “wherein is no water.” Wherein is no truth.

“Turn you to the strong hold,” The stronghold is the Bible. “ye prisoners of hope:” We are prisoners of hope, always hoping for something better. “even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee; When I have bent Judah for me,” He's going to bend Judah for him. “filled the bow with Ephraim,” Like a weapon of war. “and raised up thy sons, O Zion,” That's the rest of the tribes. “against thy sons, O Greece,” That is yet to come; this has not happened yet. “and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.” He's going to make us like the sword of a mighty man.

Them that are bound: spiritual bondage, the enslavement of sin. “The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is hid.” Say that: the iniquity of Ephraim is bound up. His sin is hid.

From here to John 8:32, because we always read that one: the truth shall make you free, and when Christ says that he's talking about two things, a literal meaning and a spiritual meaning.

sense.text: We always read this one. “And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” So when he says the truth shall make you free, he's talking about two things there: a literal meaning and a spiritual meaning.

“They answered him, We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?” So when the Pharisees heard it, they knew he was talking about captivity. They said, "We're not in bondage. We've never been in bondage to any man." Why did they say that? Because they were wealthy. They didn't see that Rome was over them taking taxes yearly; that's bondage. They didn't see it like that because they were living lively. That is that arrogant talk.

Now watch Christ's response. “Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.” See how Christ brought it into a spiritual context: if you are the servant of sin. And the result of us sinning causes what? Captivity, bondage. It's talking about the same thing, but they couldn't see that. Deuteronomy 28 shows it: slavery is a result of breaking God's commandments, and breaking God's commandments is sin.

“And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Son abideth ever.” Watch this. “If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.” Free from sin, free from bondage. He's talking about both, but they couldn't see that.

Jump to verse 32: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.” That slavery is a result of breaking God's commandments. Breaking God's commandments is sin.

sense.text:
“To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;” You know what's heavy about that? He said the good tidings, the good news, is for the meek, and those meek are those who are brokenhearted, those who are captive, those who are in prison houses and bound. Then he says in verse 2, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, meaning there is a particular year coming. Then it says the day: there's a particular day coming of vengeance. Vengeance of our God. Vengeance for what? For what we just read in verse 1. And this is what Christians can't see. So that's good news to us: God's coming to kill people to save our race. You can clap to the Lord for that thing. Y'all nervous? Hell yeah.

Vengeance: in the biblical context it refers to the act of retribution or punishment inflicted in response to wrongdoing, a theme throughout the scriptures reflecting both divine justice and human response to injustice. We always crying for justice and we never get it. Ask Rasheem Carter's mama. Ask Sonya Massey's mama. Kendrick Johnson. The concept of vengeance is closely tied to God's holiness and justice as well as the moral order he has established. The Bible frequently speaks of vengeance as belonging to God alone, Deuteronomy 32:35; see, that's why everything in these commentaries is not always right. Real Christians say vengeance is the Lord's, I will repay, saith the Lord. That's true; vengeance does start with the Lord. But once Christ smashes through the armies of this world, watch what he's going to say to us in Ezekiel 25:14. Christians don't want to hear this, but this is what the Bible says.

So there is a particular day coming that the leaders of society are aware of. Christians ignore it; they think there's going to be peace on earth, goodwill toward men all the time. No. The day of vengeance is coming: vengeance for what these nations did to our people, our twelve tribes.

Mourn: mourning in the biblical context refers to the expression of deep sorrow or grief, often associated with death, loss or repentance, a significant theme throughout the scriptures reflecting both personal and communal experiences of lamentation. Lamentations 3 gives the example of what it means to mourn: Jeremiah could not stop crying when he saw the destruction of his black people, and he had to wait for the Lord. That's what we got to do. We can't jump up and do something. When we see these images it hurts inside, it makes some of us cry, but we know we can't do nothing; we have to wait for the Lord to make his return. Before we get to Zion we are a weeping people, always going through some hardship, and God's comfort is that sorrow and mourning shall flee away when we return to the land.

precepts.why:

There's a Christian right now breaking out crying, throwing the phone at the TV screen, ripping her Bible up, throwing the church hat, kicking the shoes off. “and they shall do in Edom according to mine anger and according to my fury; and they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord God.” That's some good stuff right there. That's what we were just reading in Zechariah 9: he bends Judah and fills the bow with Ephraim. That's the vengeance. The Lord's going to get his lick first; he's going to go in there first and decimate, and then it's by the hand of his people Israel.

We're talking about vengeance. “For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever. If I whet my glittering sword,” The word whet means to sharpen: if I sharpen my glittering sword. “and mine hand take hold on judgment; I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me.” See that? And will reward them that hate me. Damn.

“I will make mine arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh; and that with the blood of the slain and of the captives, from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy.” Upon the enemy.

“Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants,” So God is going to avenge the blood of his servants. “and will render vengeance to his adversaries,” This same thing is mentioned in the book of Revelation: when they slaughter the servants of God, then the Lord's going to come. “and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people.”

Isaiah 61:2 said the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of vengeance. “For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance,” It is the day. So there is a particular day coming that the leaders of society are aware of. Christians ignore it; they think there's going to be peace on earth, goodwill toward men all the time. No. The day of vengeance is coming, vengeance for what these nations did to our people, our twelve tribes.

“and the year of recompences” Recompenses means paybacks. Payback. The big payback; the old heads know the song. “for the controversy of Zion.” Who are the Israelites, and who does that land really belong to? That is the controversy of Zion. So notice it says the day of the Lord's vengeance and the year of payback. That's what Isaiah 61:2 said. That is the same wording.

“Strengthen ye the weak hands,” So brothers, sisters, the Bible says strengthen ye the weak hands. That's you men and women: "I don't know if I can endure, I just got to commit adultery." There was a post on Facebook: a sister, and she wasn't with us, says, "I'm free from the Hebrew Israelite cult. Now I'm free in Jesus." And all her photos was her, overweight, 300 pounds in spandex with her belly out and the shoulder meat hanging. That is disgusting. There's no Israelite camp that has locks on the doors. Sisters, if it is so grievous to be a modest sister, so grievous to be a wife and a mother, take your black behind out. Go. We don't need you. We don't want you. All the doors is open; just don't come back. And you know what? They never call the Catholic Church a cult with all the rapes of children going on. They never call the Protestant churches a cult. Y'all don't see the black pastor that just got caught in the back seat having sex with a little 14-year-old boy? Nobody calls these things cults. But when you talk about Christ being black, now that's a cult. You can't make this stuff up. Our people are crazy. That's why a lot of our people, two-thirds is the exact number, got to die. So have fun out there with your female lord.

“and confirm the feeble knees.” Strengthen those knees, meaning stand up. “Say to them that are of a fearful heart,” You scared. “Be strong, fear not:” The Bible tells you to be strong; don't be afraid. “behold, your God will come with vengeance,” It's only going to get worse. You see what your president is doing? And for some reason Christians think it's all going to turn around, it's going to be oh happy day here. No. It's only going to get worse for our people. “even God with a recompence;” Payback. “he will come and save you.” You see what it says? He will come and save you. Not all. This is what we gotta remind ourselves of consistently.

Jump to verse 10 in case somebody gets simple and thinks it can be anybody. No, it's not anybody. “And the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion” Come where? To Zion. That's the land of Israel. “with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads:” There are no songs of joy over there in Israel today; you hear bullets flying and bombs dropping. But this says we're going into the land with songs and everlasting joy upon our heads. “they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.” Can't wait for that: you wake up and you got all these bills, another bill, damn; I hate that mailbox.

“Who is this that cometh from Edom,” Christ is going to come from Edom with destruction. “with dyed garments from Bozrah?” That's their capital. “this that is glorious in his apparel,” Glorious in his apparel means his garment is decked out. He ain't got a robe on; this is a decked-out garment, armor, robes, it is beautiful. “travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.” Christ said, I am mighty to save.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? I have trodden the winepress alone;” So he did the killing alone. It looked like he was stomping grapes; he did so much killing that his garment got all kinds of blood on it. “and of the people there was none with me:” He don't need our help. Christ said, I don't need the Israelites' help. “for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury;” I will tread Edom; it's talking about killing Edom. So when the Jehovah's Witnesses say Edom was already destroyed, then who is Christ coming back to kill here in Isaiah 63? You damn liars. They always lie. “and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.” Why?

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart,” Do you know the Lord is sitting on the throne beside his Father waiting for the day? Is today the day? No, son. He's just itching to come down here and stomp some people. “and the year of my redeemed is come.” Meaning our deliverance is come. That's what he's talking about.

Oh, you thought this wasn't in the New Testament. Oh yes it is. “Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you;” Never heard a church read that, and my mom used to drag us from church to church. So it's a righteous thing with God to do what? To recompense, pay back, tribulation to them that trouble you. Now you got to ask yourself, who's troubling us? Some of you are going to point to Pooky and Ray Ray. Well, Pooky and Ray Ray got that insane mentality they got because of this system. This system has warped and perverted Pooky and Ray Ray. You are a product of your environment. There was a movie on Netflix, They Cloned Tyrone: you had Tyrone, you had the hoe, and they each played a part, and that's how our people are as a whole. And also remember, Esau did very in-depth studies on our people before putting us in the ghettos and redlining and things of that nature. It's called the behavioral sink; look that up, where they did that same ghetto setup with mice. The mice began to create gangs. They began to kill one another. The male mice became effeminate, only focusing on themselves. It was everything you see in our communities. They actually did studies before setting it into place, so they already knew what was going to happen. They are the damn devil the Bible speaks of.

“And to you who are troubled rest with us,” That's the good news, and this is our message to our brothers and sisters. But they got to acknowledge and understand that they are a troubled people, a troubled race. Rest with us in these scriptures; come be comforted in these scriptures. “when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, In flaming fire taking vengeance” Taking what? Vengeance. Remember it says this is the day of vengeance, the year of vengeance: we just read that in Isaiah 61 and in Isaiah 34:8 as well. “on them that know not God,” Edom, and all who follow him too. “and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ:” That obey not the good news of our Lord Jesus Christ.

“Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power; When he shall come to be glorified in his saints,” We're the saints. “and to be admired in all them that believe (because our testimony among you was believed) in that day.”

To give us an example of what it means to mourn. “All our enemies have opened their mouths against us. Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.” Watch this. “Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water” That's crying. “for the destruction of the daughter of my people. Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not,” So the tears kept coming down Jeremiah's face; it said and ceaseth not. “without any intermission,” He could not stop crying when he saw the destruction of his black people.

When we see images like this, it hurts inside; it makes some of us cry. But we know we can't do nothing. We have to wait for the Lord to make his return.

“For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem:” So it's talking about the Israelites. “thou shalt weep no more:” See that? Letting you know that before we get to Zion, we are a weeping people. We're always going through something, some hardship. “he will be very gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee.” That's right.

“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity,” The bread of adversity is hardship, hard times. “and the water of affliction,” The waters of affliction is our tears, for what we see and what we go through. “yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers:” This is why we hit the streets all the time. This is why we have classes seven days a week, three times a day.

“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it,” Why? Because you're walking in the wrong direction. You're walking in the wrong religion. You're walking in Islam, you're walking in Christianity, some of you walking in Buddhism, some of you walking in Rastafarianism. “when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.”

“Therefore the redeemed of the Lord shall return, and come with singing unto Zion;” So we're going to return to the land with singing unto Zion. “and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away.” That is the comfort for all that mourn: the mourning flees away when we return.

sense.text:

“to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that he might be glorified.” That he might be glorified. So those lamentations, these cries, the mourning that we go through: Sonya Massey, Rasheem Carter, and Trey Reed. They turn a blind eye and say absolutely nothing about these atrocities that have been happening for however long.

Look at the names. This is why we mourn in Zion. This is why the glad tidings, the good tidings, is for us, our people. To bind up the brokenhearted: this is why we're brokenhearted. To proclaim liberty to the captives: this is captivity here, but it's become so normal to some of us that we accept this. The opening of the prison to them that are bound, to appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to comfort all that mourn. Ninety percent of these never make the news; some of these names we don't even recognize. So this ain't happening to everybody on the planet.

And one of the things we rarely talk about are black political prisoners: brothers, and some sisters, who were imprisoned back in the 60s fighting for the rights of black and brown people, and their names have virtually been forgotten. They say, "Oh no, but they killed somebody." Well, what was the cop doing? Remember the MOVE movement in 1985, where they dropped C4 on them, shot up and killed those little children, and then lied and said, "Oh no, they were shooting first." That was a lie, and the news proved it was a lie. They did the same thing with Fred Hampton. And our people will see our brothers like this and forget about them. The rights that many of us have today to run our black gums is because of these brothers and sisters that are still incarcerated to this day, and they die in prison, and black Christians who always run their black gums don't give a damn. Black political prisoners are often black activists from movements like the Black Panther Party or Black Liberation Army, unjustly incarcerated for their political beliefs, activities, or race rather than purely criminal acts: Mumia Abu-Jamal, Assata Shakur, Sundiata Acoli and Jalil Muntaqim, many serving decades for actions tied to black liberation struggles.

“And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.” You see that right there? Several times in the scriptures, when our people saw Christ, they thought that the day of vengeance was in. They thought the Lord was going to destroy Rome. See that last sentence: they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear. Acts 1:6 proves the point, and so does John the Baptist asking from prison in Matthew 11.

Everybody thought it was going to be the same thing. Nobody wanted to hear the sacrifice stuff. All Israel wanted the deliverance part, the vengeance part, but that was not the time.

precepts.why: Just to prove the point. “When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” See that? They thought it was in: will you restore the kingdom to Israel? Now how come the churches don't read that and go, "No, they made a mistake. It's for everybody"? The hell is this?

Here's another one, with John the Baptist. And anybody that thinks John the Baptist was a wicked negro, you're on crack. “Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?” Why'd he ask that? John was in prison. He thought deliverance was at that time. That's why he was talking greasy to Herod: remember Herod walked in with his brother's wife and John was bold, it's unlawful for you to have your brother's wife, and they arrested him and put him in jail. So he's thinking, I'm good, Christ is going to deliver me out of here. But that wasn't the time.

“Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:” To encourage John. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.” Here it comes. “And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.” He was telling John, don't be offended, because this is not the time for deliverance. This is the time for me to be sacrificed. Everybody thought it was going to be the same thing; nobody wanted to hear the sacrifice stuff. All Israel wanted the deliverance part, the vengeance part, but that was not the time.

sense.text: Read above verse 14 so we know the context. “Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist:” Christ said there's nobody greater than John the Baptist. “notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.” Why? Because in the kingdom of heaven, when you read Isaiah, all Israel shall be all righteous: no fears, no more sin. That's why the least in the kingdom is going to be greater than John was at that time.

“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence,” By Rome, at the hands of Rome. “and the violent take it by force.” How did Rome get over Jerusalem? Around 63 BC General Pompey came in with a whole military and took Jerusalem, took the land of Israel. That's how Rome got their foothold on the land, so that's why when Christ was born they all had to pay taxes to Caesar.

The violence wasn't up in the sky. The violence was to the kingdom of heaven on earth, letting you know that we are the kingdom of heaven. The violent: he's calling Rome the violent. The white man is the violent man.

“For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.” So Christ revealed that John the Baptist was who? Elijah. This goes for brothers out there saying John the Baptist was wicked; Matthew 17 settles it.

precepts.why:
This goes for brothers out there saying John the Baptist was wicked. John the Baptist by this time had gotten killed already, but now Christ knew his crucifixion was coming, and look what happened. Remember John is dead already.

“And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart, And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.” Watch this. “And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.” So John the Baptist was talking to Christ with Moses. How you going to read that and go, "Oh, he was wicked"? You are stupid as hell; something's wrong with you. John got killed already, and now in the spirit realm the disciples saw Christ speaking with Moses and John the Baptist, Elijah. You can't make this stuff up.

sense.text: “because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.” They all thought deliverance was coming right then, at that time. Paul had to make it sure and certain in 2 Thessalonians 2: this is not the time. Christ ain't coming in this time period. Things got to happen: all Israel got to fall and go into captivity, and the man of sin got to be revealed. Nobody wanted to hear that.

“He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.” So this certain nobleman is Christ. What does it mean when it says he went into a far country? Acts 1:9: he was taken up and a cloud received him out of their sight. So he went into the heavens, to the true tabernacle. That's where Christ went.

“And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.” The servants: Isaiah 41:8, thou Israel art my servant. Everybody's not the servants of the Lord. The Christians just get on my nerve with their lies, "everybody's the servants of the Lord." No, they're not. Leviticus 25:55: unto me the children of Israel are servants.

The ten pounds: pounds is money. What is it going into? Psalms 119:127, I love thy commandments above gold, above fine gold. So these pounds represent something so precious, which is the word of God, the commandments. Occupy till I come.

“But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.” So the citizens that hated him: Mark 8:31 says who hated Christ. You hear Christians go, "He came unto his own and his own received him not." Shut up. That ain't talking about all the Israelites. The Son of man was rejected of the elders and of the chief priests and scribes. That's who hated Christ. That's who rejected him.

“And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom,” Hold that. There's a lot implied in that. If you don't read the Old Testament prophecies, you'll just read this parable and go, "Oh yeah, he just came back to the kingdom." No, a lot took place between that. Isaiah 66:15-17: the Lord will come with fire, and the slain of the Lord shall be many. Christ is going to kill a lot of people to receive his kingdom. Revelation 12:7-10: war in heaven, and then, now is come salvation and the kingdom of our God. That's the receiving of the kingdom. There's going to be war and turmoil before that comes.

“then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.” He wanted to know, what did you do with the understanding I imparted to you? What did you do with it? We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, every man, every woman, and this is what the parable's talking about. Every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

“Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds. And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much. Have thou authority over ten cities: Revelation 2:26, to him will I give power over the nations, and he shall rule them with a rod of iron.

Look at what he's actually saying. You know how difficult it is with your family: you family men trying to get your wife to come to this truth, your kids out of order, you got to try to get the household together. Now imagine trying to organize a whole city, and not just one city, ten cities. Christ said you have authority over ten cities. That means you got to teach them the dietary law, moral law, civil law, ceremonial law. You got to teach them all that. And there's going to be people that buck up: "I ain't doing what you say." Oh, is that right? That's when Revelation 2:26 comes in, because they got to be broken down. So it ain't no easy task.

“And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.” Matthew 13:12: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance. That's the top part. But look at the second part: whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath. We get to that with the servant who kept his pound in a napkin.

“And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:” He kept it laid up in a napkin. Romans 12:11: not slothful in business, in God's business, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord. John 15:2: every branch in me that beareth not fruit, you are unproductive, he taketh away; he'll kill you. Ecclesiasticus 32:17: a sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will. Them old excuse makers. That's what this servant is doing.

“For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man:” Look up that word austere: stern and cold in appearance or manner. Christ was a cold brother. Somber. Grave. Morally strict. Damn, that's it, that one right there: morally strict. So the guy that's making excuses says, you're morally strict, you cold. “thou takest up that thou layedst not down,” Because Christ ain't on the earth doing the work. It's you men. “and reapest that thou didst not sow.” And he's going to reap the benefits.

“And he saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant.” What did he call him? Thou wicked servant. So sometimes people think, especially men, "I could be an Israelite and I don't have to do nothing." It called him a wicked servant. “Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow:” Ezekiel 20:44: not according to your wicked ways, nor according to your corrupt doings, O ye house of Israel. So we have had corrupt doings. This servant was very corrupt.

“Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank,” The bank is this truth. The bank is this congregation. The bank is whatever congregations we have. That is the bank. Romans 12:6: we all have gifts, differing according to the grace given to us; if your gift is prophecy, prophesy according to the proportion of faith. So let's say you can break down Deuteronomy 28; that's as far as your gift goes, then do that, use that. You might not know 2 Esdras 12; don't even try to get into that. Prophesy according to the proportion of faith God gave you. But damn it, do something. Don't just sit around doing nothing. Now, I'm not talking about if you are handicapped or crippled, or you're very up in age; there's other things you can do. But shoot, I've seen brothers in wheelchairs at camp giving out flyers. The hell you talking about?

precepts.why:

People going around saying this is the time, this is the time. Paul had to make it sure and certain: this is not the time.

The servants. “But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.” Everybody's not the servants of the Lord.

The Christians just get on my nerve with their lies: "Everybody's the servants of the Lord." No, they're not. “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” So everybody is not the servants of the Lord. The ten servants are Israel.

The ten pounds. Pounds is money; this is money. What is it going into? “Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.” So these pounds represent something so precious, which is the word of God, the commandments.

The citizens that hated him: who hated Christ? You hear Christians go, "He came unto his own and his own received him not." Shut up. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” So Christ is going to kill a lot of people to receive his kingdom.

It's going to be a lot of killing.

Showing you what happens before he takes the kingdom. “And there was war in heaven:” There was what? War in heaven. “Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,” So Satan is going to fight against Michael and his angels. So Satan's going to have who? America, Europe, China, Russia; they're all going to fight against the Lord. “And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven. And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.”

That's the receiving of the kingdom. So there's going to be war and turmoil before that comes.

That he might know how much every man had gained by trading: what did you do with the understanding I imparted to you? “Wherefore we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.” We all want to be accepted of Christ. “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ;” Every man, every woman. And this is what the parable's talking about: what did you do with what I gave you? “that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” Whether it be good or bad.
“So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.” That's right. Every servant is called to account for what he did with the pounds.

This is what the servant with the napkin is doing. “A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” Them old excuse makers.

Thou wicked servant. “And ye shall know that I am the Lord, when I have wrought with you for my name’s sake, not according to your wicked ways, nor according to your corrupt doings, O ye house of Israel, saith the Lord God.” So we have had corrupt dealings, corrupt doings. This servant was very corrupt.

So let's say, for example, you can break down Deuteronomy 28; that's as far as your gift goes, then do that, use that. You might not know 2 Esdras 12; don't even try to get into that. Prophesy according to the proportion of faith God gave you. But damn it, do something. Don't just sit around and do nothing. Now, I'm not talking about if you are handicapped or crippled, or you're very up in age; there's other things you can do. But shoot, I've seen brothers in wheelchairs at camp giving out flyers. The hell you talking about?

sense.text: “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth;” So in this great house, which is the twelve tribes of Israel, which we are part of, there are vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and of earth. They know who they are.

Some circles, women just gossip; gossip girls, you got to know: I got to separate from the sister right here. Or the sister that always disrespects her husband, and you know she disrespects her husband, but she's your friend. The decent sister thinks her giving her scripture is going to rub off on the hard-headed sister. It don't happen that way. It's the other way around: the way of the wicked seduceth them.

precepts.why: "No, Bishop, I think I could win her over." Yes, she knows better than God. “The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.” If you hang around wicked people, you will be seduced. So you hang around a girl that gossips, you hang around a girl that disrespects her husband, don't even feed her kids, and that's your friend. And then sure enough, she goes home one day and disrespects her husband. I wonder why it happened like that. And now we're the cult.

For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.” That's what we just read in Matthew 13:12, saying the same thing.

So the one that had one pound and didn't do anything was supposed to have authority over one city, and the Lord said, take that city and give it to the one that has ten cities.
